title: Adjectives + that-clause or to-infinitive
summary: Как выбирать между **adjective + that-clause** и **adjective + to-infinitive** (**sure that / sure to**, **glad to / glad that**), сослагательное **It is essential that he be...** и конструкции вроде **easy to use**.
ru:
## Две конструкции — две точки зрения
После многих прилагательных можно поставить и **that-clause**, и **to-инфинитив**, но смысл различается. Инфинитив обычно связан с **подлежащим** (именно оно действует или переживает), а that-клауза вводит **самостоятельный факт**.
> I'm **sorry to hear** that you're leaving. — Мне жаль слышать (я узнаю это сейчас).
> I'm **sorry that** you're leaving. — Мне жаль, что вы уходите.
> She was **surprised to find** the door open. — Она удивилась, обнаружив дверь открытой (сама обнаружила).
> She was **surprised that** the door was open. — Её удивило, что дверь была открыта.

## Прилагательные только с одной из конструкций
Это то, что надо запоминать: **likely, bound, liable, due, apt** строятся с инфинитивом (**certain, sure** — с обеими конструкциями, см. ниже), а **aware, convinced, conscious, doubtful** — that-клаузу.
> The project is **likely to** be delayed. = **It is likely that** the project will be delayed.
> They're **bound to** notice. — Они обязательно заметят.
> I'm **aware that** this is a sensitive matter. — Я осознаю, что это деликатный вопрос.
- ~~She is probable to win.~~ → She is **likely** to win. / It is **probable** that she'll win.
- ~~I'm convinced to be right.~~ → I'm convinced **that** I'm right.

## sure, certain, afraid: перемена смысла
> He is **sure to** win. — Он наверняка победит (мнение говорящего).
> He is **sure that** he'll win. — Он уверен, что победит (уверенность самого подлежащего).
> I'm **afraid to** ask. — Боюсь спрашивать (меня останавливает страх).
> I'm **afraid that** we've missed it. — Боюсь, что мы это упустили (мягкое сожаление).

## It is essential that he be... — сослагательное
После прилагательных важности и рекомендации (**essential, vital, important, necessary, desirable, advisable, crucial**) в формальном стиле возможна **that-клауза без -s**: *that he be, that she attend*. В британском варианте обычнее **should**, в американском — голая форма; в разговорной речи часто просто обычное время.
> It is **vital that** every user **be** informed. (формально)
> It is vital that every user **should be** informed. (BrE)
> It's vital that every user **is** informed. (разг.)
> It was **essential that** she **not** be disturbed. — Было необходимо, чтобы её не беспокоили.

## «Пассивные» инфинитивы
С прилагательными трудности и качества инфинитив имеет страдательный смысл, а дополнение стоит перед прилагательным.
> The software is **easy to use**. — Программой легко пользоваться. (~~easy to use it~~)
> He is **hard to please**. — Ему трудно угодить.
> This water is **safe to drink**. — Эту воду можно пить.
> The house is **ideal to live in**, **great to look at**. — Дом идеален для жизни; на него приятно смотреть (предлог остаётся в конце).

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~It is important him to know.~~ → It is important **for him** to know.
- ~~The task is difficult to do it.~~ → The task is difficult **to do**.
- ~~I'm glad that to see you.~~ → I'm glad **to see** you. / I'm glad **that** you came.
en:
## Two patterns, two viewpoints
Many adjectives take either a **that-clause** or a **to-infinitive**, but the meaning often differs. An infinitive usually links to the **subject** (who acts or feels), while a that-clause presents an **independent fact**.
> I'm **sorry to hear** that you're leaving. (I have just learned it.)
> I'm **sorry that** you're leaving.
> She was **surprised to find** the door open. (she found it herself)
> She was **surprised that** the door was open.

## Adjectives that prefer one pattern
**likely, bound, liable, due, apt** take the infinitive (**certain, sure** take both patterns, see below); **aware, convinced, conscious, doubtful** take a that-clause.
> The project is **likely to** be delayed. = **It is likely that** the project will be delayed.
> They're **bound to** notice.
> I'm **aware that** this is a sensitive matter.
- ~~She is probable to win.~~ → She is **likely** to win. / It is **probable** that she'll win.
- ~~I'm convinced to be right.~~ → I'm convinced **that** I'm right.

## sure, certain, afraid: change of meaning
> He is **sure to** win. (the speaker is certain)
> He is **sure that** he'll win. (he himself is confident)
> I'm **afraid to** ask. (fear stops me)
> I'm **afraid that** we've missed it. (polite regret)

## It is essential that he be... the subjunctive
After adjectives of importance (**essential, vital, important, necessary, desirable, advisable, crucial**) formal English allows a that-clause with the bare form: *that he be, that she attend*. British English often prefers **should**, American English the bare form, and casual speech the normal tense.
> It is **vital that** every user **be** informed. (formal)
> It is vital that every user **should be** informed. (BrE)
> It's vital that every user **is** informed. (informal)
> It was **essential that** she **not** be disturbed.

## 'Passive' infinitives
After adjectives of difficulty and quality the infinitive has a passive meaning, and the object does not repeat.
> The software is **easy to use**. (~~easy to use it~~)
> He is **hard to please**.
> This water is **safe to drink**.
> The house is **ideal to live in**, **great to look at**. (the preposition stays)

## Common mistakes
- ~~It is important him to know.~~ → It is important **for him** to know.
- ~~The task is difficult to do it.~~ → The task is difficult **to do**.
- ~~I'm glad that to see you.~~ → I'm glad **to see** you. / I'm glad **that** you came.
structure:
## Схемы
> подлежащее + be + прилагательное + **to-инфинитив**: She is **eager to start**.
> подлежащее + be + прилагательное + **(that)** + клауза: She is **aware (that)** time is short.
> **It is** + прилагательное + **that** + клауза: **It is odd that** nobody called.
> **It is** + прилагательное + **for** + кто-то + **to-инфинитив**: **It is vital for us to** agree.
> **It is** + essential/vital + **that** + подлежащее + **(should) + голая форма**: **It is essential that** he **(should) attend**.

## Таблица: прилагательные и конструкции
| Группа | Прилагательные | Пример |
|---|---|---|
| Эмоции | glad, sorry, relieved, delighted, surprised | I'm **relieved to know** / **that** you are safe. |
| Вероятность | likely, unlikely, certain, sure, bound | She is **bound to** call. |
| Готовность | eager, willing, reluctant, ready, keen | He is **reluctant to** speak. |
| Знание | aware, conscious, convinced, doubtful | I'm **convinced that** it works. |
| Важность | essential, vital, crucial, necessary | It is **crucial that** he **be** present. |
| Трудность | easy, hard, difficult, impossible, safe | The text is **hard to read**. |

exercises.title: to-инфинитив или that
exercises.instruction: Вставьте слова, чтобы получилось естественное предложение. Если в скобках глагол — поставьте его в нужную форму (to-инфинитив, а после *essential that* — сослагательное наклонение).

items.text: I was sorry {{to hear}} that your flight was cancelled.
She's determined {{to finish}} her degree this year.
He is certain {{that}} the money was transferred on Friday.
The report is likely {{to cause}} controversy.
It is essential that every applicant {{be|should be|is}} interviewed in person.
Don't drink the water from that stream; it isn't safe {{to drink}}.
She was surprised {{to find}} the door open.
They are bound {{to notice}} the mistake.
We were thrilled {{to}} see the results.
I'm convinced {{that}} the figures are wrong.
She is eager {{to}} start the new job.
I'm aware {{that}} this is a sensitive issue.
He was too proud {{to}} ask for help.
Are you sure {{that}} the meeting is today?
They are unlikely {{to}} agree to these terms.
It's unfortunate {{that}} we missed the deadline.

exercises.title: easy to use
exercises.instruction: Вставьте инфинитив с **to** от глагола в скобках; предлог после пропуска уже есть в тексте, если он нужен.

items.text: The new app is really easy {{to use}}.
Her handwriting is impossible {{to read}}.
The lake is too cold {{to swim}} in.
He is a hard man {{to please}}.
This is a difficult text {{to translate}}.
The sauce is delicious, but it's hard {{to make}}.
The software is free {{to download}}.

items.q: I'm afraid ___ the delay will cost us the contract.
It is vital that she ___ informed immediately.
I was sorry ___ that you had been ill.
She is anxious ___ everything goes smoothly.

exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение с прилагательным и to-инфинитивом.

answers: I was surprised to see her there.

items.prompt: It is certain that the price will rise. → The price ...
answers: The price is certain to rise.

items.prompt: It's likely that they will refuse. → They ...
answers: They are likely to refuse.

items.prompt: It is essential that all passengers fasten their seat belts. (for) → It is essential ...

items.prompt: She was relieved when she heard that the results were good. → She was relieved ...

answers: This app is easy to use.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя прилагательное + to-инфинитив или that-клауза.

items.prompt: What are you eager or reluctant to do this year?
items.sample: I'm eager to start learning German, but I'm reluctant to give up my free weekends.

items.prompt: Name something you were relieved or surprised to learn recently.
items.sample: I was relieved to learn that the exam had been postponed.

items.prompt: What is essential for a good team? Use: It is essential that ...
items.sample: It is essential that everyone be honest about their mistakes.

items.prompt: Describe something in your life that is easy or hard to do.
items.sample: My old car is hard to start in winter.
